facts.claim: The reportInteraction event name diverges from the DashboardInteractions method/property name: the helper is `textPanelUsage` emitting `text_panel_usage`, but tests assert on `dashboards_text_panel_usage`, indicating the actual shipped event name differs from what's declared in interactions.ts.
facts.evidence: `reportDashboardInteraction('text_panel_usage', properties);` in interactions.ts vs `expect(reportInteraction).toHaveBeenCalledWith('dashboards_text_panel_usage', ...)` in tracking.test.ts

facts.claim: Feature-usage tracking for text panel features must be gated behind both relevant feature flags (new text panel v2 AND new text features) since usage counting logic (mermaid/handlebars/etc.) only applies meaningfully when both are enabled; omitting either flag check would misattribute usage from the old panel or unreleased features.
facts.evidence: `flags.getBooleanValue(FlagKeys.GrafanaNewTextPanel, false) && flags.getBooleanValue(FlagKeys.TextNewFeatures, false)` and test cases `it.each([['the v2 panel is off', ...], ['the new features are off', ...], ['both flags are off', {}]])` that all assert no reporting occurs

facts.claim: Mermaid/handlebars pattern detection must be skipped when the text panel is in `TextMode.Code`, because code mode renders raw text without interpreting markdown/mermaid syntax, so counting matches there would overcount features that never actually render.
facts.evidence: `if (options.mode !== TextMode.Code) { if (MERMAID_PATTERN.test(content)) ... if (HANDLEBARS_PATTERN.test(content)) ... }` and test `'does not count diagrams or templates in code mode, where neither one renders'`

json.reason: The PR adds a non-trivial, non-obvious tracking mechanism with specific constraints: dual feature-flag gating logic, mode-dependent pattern matching (code mode suppresses detection), and a naming mismatch between the interactions.ts event string and what the tests actually assert, which is a concrete, reusable discrepancy worth flagging for future reviewers/maintainers of this file.
